ClientResponses.Response:
Your feedback is very important to us. We are so sorry to hear about your grill not going past 200. We are here to help.

If you are using your grill with the adapter hose to a larger 20 lb. refill/exchange LP tank, it sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.
Open the lid
Make sure the control knob is in the off position
Turn your LP tank on all the way
Wait 60 seconds
Turn the burner to start/high (first position to the left)
Hit your igniter
Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F
For troubleshooting purposes, I would suggest using your grill with a 14 or 16 oz. disposable LP cylinder as well. That will let you know right away if the issue is with the grill, or with the adapter hose/LP tank. 

Our Care team will reach out to follow up. Please look for an outreach email from us soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: For many years, I had a large gas grill that served us well. However, since there’s only my wife and me at home now, we just needed a smaller grill and the Weber Q1200 has proven to be the ideal choice. It’s a great size to cook everything we need, the coated grates are very easy to clean up  (I just soak them in water for several hours and then all of the cooking residue comes off easily). The only downside I’ve experienced was the sudden death of the gas regulator. However, the Weber Tech folks talked me through the full troubleshooting to determine that it was the regulator that had failed. Amazon provided a replacement part which was only $43 compared to Webber’s $79 cost.  (Sorry Weber). Otherwise, this little Weber Grill has proven to be a great choice.
